youtube.title: Chernobyl's Emergency Button Helped Blow It Up. The Flaw Was Known 3 Years Earlier
youtube.description:
At 1:23 a.m. on 26 April 1986, Chernobyl's operators pressed AZ-5, the emergency shutdown button. The graphite tips of the control rods briefly pushed power up at the bottom of the core, and the reactor exploded seconds later. The 'positive scram' effect had been identified at Ignalina in 1983; restrictions were supposed to follow but never did, and the operators were not clearly told.

📂 Case File #045: The Chernobyl Button
